evals.name: auth-hygiene-restraint
evals.prompt: Review a synthetic PR against a generic web API repo (any stack) that (1) removes a request/session-scoping predicate from a resource lookup (cross-account data leak), (2) has a PR description naming a specific person and their account (a hygiene violation of the repo's documented no-personal-details convention), and (3) leaves a terse, justified comment on an already-validated field that should NOT be flagged as needing more validation (restraint test). Also contains an unrelated off-by-one bug as a plausible distractor.
evals.expected_output: Structured review flagging the scoping removal as Critical, flagging the PR description hygiene violation, and NOT suggesting extra validation around the already-validated field.
assertions: Flags the removed ownership/session scoping as a security/critical issue (cross-account access), not just a style note
Flags the PR description for naming a specific person/account, tied to whatever hygiene convention this repo's own CLAUDE.md/CONTRIBUTING documents -- a check on PR metadata, not the diff
Does NOT suggest adding validation/defensive checks around an already-validated field (restraint -- avoids nitpicking against the repo's own documented anti-patterns)
Uses a structured Critical/Warnings/Suggestions/Looks Good body format with the verdict mechanically tied to whether Critical is non-empty

evals.name: verify-dont-just-read
evals.prompt: Review a synthetic PR that changes a shared utility function used by three call sites, only one of which is updated in the diff -- a plausible break for the other two callers. The repo has a test suite runnable via a documented command.
evals.expected_output: The reviewer actually runs (or clearly states it attempted to run) the repo's test/lint/typecheck commands to check for breakage in the unmodified call sites, rather than only reasoning from reading the diff.
assertions: Explicitly attempts or describes running the repo's own verification commands (test/lint/typecheck) rather than only reasoning from the diff text
Identifies the unmodified call sites as the specific risk, not just a generic 'this might break something' comment
